sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Text patterns for tags and locations
sections.what: Holds the patterns for hyphen tags, dotted tokens, chainage, grid references, levels, from-to routes, activity code prefixes and compound codes.
sections.why: Likely reason: these patterns find the location and tag clues that schedules store as plain text.
sections.watch_out: Patterns are loose; the level pattern, for example, can match a short letter and number that is not a level.

sections.name: grouping_values
sections.title: Group labels for each activity
sections.what: Returns one group label per strategy for an activity, covering work breakdown depth, tags, chainage, grid, level, route, the first name fields, and the code prefix and compound code.
sections.why: Likely reason: each grouping method needs one label per activity, so the scorer can compare them fairly.
sections.watch_out: Only the first match of each pattern is kept, and labels are capitalised and shortened, so renaming a strategy changes what is saved.

summary: Reads each activity's name, path and code, and pulls out the possible group labels it could be filed under, such as its work breakdown levels, tags, chainage, grid references and code prefixes.
purpose: Creates the candidate groupings that the service later scores to pick the best one for building the 3D model.
why: Likely reason: schedules do not carry one standard grouping, so several possible groupings are collected and then judged.
how: Splits the work breakdown path into levels and records each level. Then searches the name and path for tags, chainage, grid references, levels and from-to routes, and records the first match of each. It then splits the name into fields and records the first few, and finally reads the activity code and records its prefix and compound form.
inputs: One normalized activity with its name, work breakdown path and activity code.
outputs: A dictionary that maps a strategy name to one group label for that activity. Strategy names describe the kind of grouping, such as depth in the path or a chainage.
risks: The patterns are loose, so unrelated text may be read as a tag, grid or level. Labels are shortened and capitalised, so two different values may merge.
debug: Check the group labels produced for one activity first. If a tag looks wrong, test the matching pattern against that activity's name and path. If a grouping is missing, confirm the activity has the expected text.
